summary: Interrogated the FORGE-UPG-1 draft against the roadmap story's seven acceptance criteria, every ID from `forge decision list --active`, and docs/specs/legacy-upgrade.md. One blocking gap: the plan's own remedy did not actually work in sequence. Resolved in the plan text.
gaps: BLOCKING: `stage migrate --base` does not by itself make a legacy stage closable, so the plan did not deliver the outcome it justified itself by. Walked through: migrate stamps base_sha AND task_sha256 together; agentstats' legacy contract is prose and must be re-recorded; the new digest makes _measure refuse 'contract changed after the stage started'; the only sanctioned repair is `stage start`, which re-baselines base_sha to HEAD and destroys the migrated base; the stage then closes on an empty diff and is refused again. The plan named the destination and not the route.

The Verify Plan asserted agentstats ends in a good state without saying what AGS-13.2's re-recorded contract declares. Its only evidence was a live production transcript, and the new required_tests contract takes runner-owned {id, path, command} proofs — so the criterion was unfalsifiable as written.
resolutions: Risks section rewritten to state the ordering constraint as the finding, not a footnote: re-record the decomposition FIRST, then `stage migrate`, so base_sha and the current task digest are stamped in the same act. No code change — the defect was in the sequence, and adding a refusal for the wrong order would be building a guard against a mistake the plan now simply does not make.

Verify Plan step 3 now spells the agentstats sequence out in order and names the contract: empty required_tests with the repo's real runner as the single verify command. Put to the human, who chose it over writing a retroactive vitest case or parking the stage as --incomplete. The production transcript stays in the recorded testing artifact, which is what it was always evidence for.
open_items: Non-blocking: two tasks rather than one. They are ~30 lines each and share factory/tests/test_gates.py, so a single task was the simpler shape considered. Kept split because they decompose by concern (vendoring migration vs stage measurement) rather than by file count, and each closes on an independently measurable diff.

Non-blocking: no escape flag for a harness release that RETIRES a script, which would abort carry-then-verify on older repos. Named as a known ceiling in Risks with the refusal telling the human to delete the retired file and re-run. Verified against the real target: all 65 files under agentstats' .agents/ have a counterpart, so the abort does not fire today.
Non-blocking: `forge findings patterns` reports one finding class, none recurring — no consolidation or tripwire owed by this story.
